title: Generate Trajectories, Reasoning Traces, and Auto-Labels with NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Super | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA is releasing Alpamayo 2 Super, a 34B open reasoning vision-language-action model for autonomous driving (32B Cosmos 3 Super Reasoner plus a 2B diffusion Action Expert), under the permissive OpenMDW-1.1 license that allows commercial redistribution of distilled models without NVIDIA's permission. The benchmark disclosure is unusually candid: it tops LingoQA at 79.2 across 37 models and crushes Qwen3-VL 32B on grounding (0.71 vs 0.17 IoU), but its 6.4s minADE_6 of 0.911m barely improves on the far smaller Alpamayo 1.5 Nano's 0.916m and it loses AV reasoning to GPT-5.5 (0.433 vs 0.502).

themes.theme: Open weights as an AV land grab

insights.claim: Alpamayo 2 Super is released under OpenMDW-1.1, the Linux Foundation permissive license, explicitly covering fine-tuning, derivative models, and commercial redistribution, with model outputs carrying no license conditions.
insights.speaker: Boris Ivanovic
insights.so_what: A no-strings commercial license on a frontier AV foundation model destroys the licensing revenue model of independent AV-software vendors and pressures anyone selling proprietary driving stacks.
insights.quote: Distilled models can be deployed commercially without further permission from NVIDIA, and model outputs carry no license conditions.
insights.locator: The model weights are available on Hugging Face

insights.claim: The stated commercial endgame is distillation into compact models that run on NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor inside the vehicle, making the free 34B model a funnel into in-car NVIDIA silicon.
insights.speaker: Boris Ivanovic
insights.so_what: The giveaway is teacher-model software; the monetization is DRIVE AGX Thor design wins per vehicle — track OEM Thor adoption, not Alpamayo downloads.
insights.quote: As a teacher model, it can be distilled into compact models that run on NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor inside the vehicle.
insights.locator: Build with Alpamayo 2 Super

insights.claim: NVIDIA positions one foundation model as replacing the separate models AV teams maintain for trajectory generation, intent prediction, scene understanding, and data labeling across the development workflow.
insights.speaker: Boris Ivanovic
insights.so_what: Collapsing four internal model teams into one foundation model is a headcount and tooling-spend argument aimed directly at AV program budgets.
insights.quote: The same foundation model can be used as an offline policy teacher, an evaluation critic, a data engine, or a starting point for new task customization
insights.locator: This multi-task design gives AV developers

insights.claim: Alpamayo 2 Super is architecturally a Cosmos derivative — a 32B Cosmos 3 Super Reasoner paired with a 2B diffusion-based Action Expert, post-trained with reinforcement learning.
insights.speaker: Boris Ivanovic
insights.so_what: Autonomous driving and robotics are converging on the same Cosmos backbone, meaning NVIDIA amortizes one pretraining run across two large physical-AI markets.
insights.locator: NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Super is an open 34-billion-parameter

insights.claim: The 34B model's 6.4-second minADE_6 of 0.911m on 1,434 challenging Physical AI AV Dataset samples barely improves on Alpamayo 1.5 Nano's 0.916m, meaning a large parameter increase bought roughly 5mm of trajectory accuracy.
insights.speaker: Boris Ivanovic
insights.so_what: Trajectory accuracy appears to be saturating against scale — evidence that AV progress now depends on reasoning and long-tail handling rather than bigger planners.
insights.locator: Trajectory prediction: Across 1,434 challenging samples

insights.claim: On the Physical AI AV Reasoning Benchmark, Alpamayo 2 Super scores 0.433 versus GPT-5.5 at 0.502, so a general-purpose frontier LLM still beats NVIDIA's domain-specific driving model on AV reasoning.
insights.speaker: Boris Ivanovic
insights.so_what: Domain specialization is not yet beating general frontier scale on reasoning quality — a data point against the thesis that vertical AV models will dominate.
insights.locator: Table 1. Open-loop and closed-loop evaluation

insights.claim: Alpamayo 2 Super ranks first among 37 evaluated models on LingoQA at 79.2, leading Qwen2.5-VL 72B by 17.0 points, Qwen3-VL 32B by 7.0, Gemini 2.5 Pro by 15.1, and GPT-4o by 23.2, at less than half the parameter count of the largest competitor.
insights.speaker: Boris Ivanovic
insights.so_what: Beating Gemini 2.5 Pro and GPT-4o on driving-scene QA with 34B open weights shows domain post-training beats raw scale for narrow visual reasoning — the efficient path for vertical AI.
insights.quote: With 34 billion parameters, it leads Qwen2.5-VL (72B) by 17.0 points, Qwen3-VL (32B) by 7.0 points, Gemini 2.5 Pro by 15.1 points, and GPT-4o by 23.2 points.
insights.locator: LingoQA

insights.claim: The closed-loop AlpaSim Score on 913 reconstructed scenes is 1.50 plus or minus 0.13 versus Alpamayo 1.5 Nano's 1.37 plus or minus 0.10 — a roughly 9% gain whose error bars nearly overlap.
insights.speaker: Boris Ivanovic
insights.so_what: Overlapping confidence intervals on the headline closed-loop metric mean the generational improvement is directional rather than decisive.
insights.locator: On 913 reconstructed scenes

insights.claim: The article reports an identical 0.652 similarity score against an identical Qwen3-VL 32B baseline of 0.450 for two different tasks — VQA answer quality on 8K QA pairs and CoC auto-labeling on 8k clips — a suspicious duplication that warrants verification.
insights.speaker: Boris Ivanovic
insights.so_what: Either a copy-paste error or coincidence; either way, treat the auto-labeling quality claim as unverified when assessing the annotation-cost argument.
insights.quote: Alpamayo 2 Super achieves a 0.652 similarity score, compared with Qwen3-VL 32B at 0.450.
insights.locator: Evaluate CoC auto-labeling quality

insights.claim: Meta-action prediction accuracy is markedly uneven across the taxonomy — 74.59 lateral IoU and 73.55 lane-wise IoU but only 61.91 longitudinal IoU on 94K internally labeled clips.
insights.speaker: Boris Ivanovic
insights.so_what: Longitudinal decisions (stop, accelerate, yield timing) are the weakest axis and also the safety-critical one — the specific gap to watch in the next release.
insights.locator: On an internal set of 94K clips

insights.claim: Open-loop evaluation compares predictions to a fixed prerecorded future and therefore cannot capture how the scene changes after the model's first action, systematically hiding the failures that matter.
insights.speaker: Boris Ivanovic
insights.so_what: Any AV company citing only open-loop trajectory error is reporting a metric that structurally cannot detect its policy's real-world failure modes.
insights.quote: they evaluate predictions against a fixed, prerecorded future and therefore don’t capture what happens after the model’s first action
insights.locator: The main challenge with open-loop metrics

insights.claim: The concrete failure illustration is that in open-loop replay an adjacent vehicle continues its recorded path when the ego changes lanes, rather than reacting — an artifact that flatters lane-change performance.
insights.speaker: Boris Ivanovic
insights.so_what: A crisp diagnostic to apply to any AV benchmark claim: ask whether other agents react.
insights.locator: For example, if the ego vehicle changes lanes

insights.claim: NVIDIA AlpaSim executes each predicted action within the scene with reactive behavior models, revealing collisions, road departures, and close encounters that can only emerge once the policy influences future observations.
insights.speaker: Boris Ivanovic
insights.so_what: Owning the closed-loop simulator alongside the model gives NVIDIA control of the evaluation standard the AV industry is being pushed toward.
insights.quote: This closed-loop score complements open-loop results by revealing collisions, road departures, close encounters, and other failures that can emerge only after the policy influences future observations.
insights.locator: On 913 reconstructed scenes

themes.theme: Interpretability wired into the safety case

insights.claim: The model jointly emits a trajectory and a Chain-of-Causation reasoning trace, allowing teams to diagnose whether a failure originated in perception, reasoning, or action generation rather than treating the policy as a black box.
insights.speaker: Boris Ivanovic
insights.so_what: Attributable failure modes are what regulators and insurers need; interpretability is becoming a compliance feature rather than a research nicety.
insights.quote: The trajectory expresses what the ego vehicle could do next. The CoC reasoning trace provides insights into why a driving decision was made from observed scene context.
insights.locator: Trajectories and CoC traces: What and why

insights.claim: CoC traces feed directly into NVIDIA Halos safety validation workflows by enabling introspection into the model's scene understanding, linking the open model to NVIDIA's safety-certification tooling.
insights.speaker: Boris Ivanovic
insights.so_what: If Halos becomes the de facto AV safety validation path, NVIDIA controls the certification bottleneck as well as the compute and the model.
insights.locator: CoC traces also feed into the NVIDIA Halos

insights.claim: Meta-actions such as yield, change lanes, stop, and accelerate are proposed as the bridge between an end-to-end foundation model and a legacy modular AV stack, letting a downstream planner consume the decision.
insights.speaker: Boris Ivanovic
insights.so_what: This is the migration path for OEMs with existing rule-based planners — adoption need not be a rip-and-replace, which materially widens the near-term market.
insights.quote: These outputs can help bridge an end-to-end foundation model and a modular AV stack
insights.locator: Meta-actions

insights.claim: 2D grounding lets the model spatially localize the actors it references with bounding boxes, so reviewers can verify which object the model means and automated checks can flag missing or inconsistent boxes.
insights.speaker: Boris Ivanovic
insights.so_what: Grounding turns model explanations from unfalsifiable text into auditable claims — the difference between marketing interpretability and usable interpretability.
insights.quote: This grounding makes outputs more useful than free-form text alone.
insights.locator: Querying multi-camera scenes with VQA and 2D grounding

insights.claim: On 2D grounding IoU, Alpamayo 2 Super scores 0.71 versus 0.17 for Qwen3-VL 32B, a more than fourfold gap that dwarfs the differences on any text-based metric.
insights.speaker: Boris Ivanovic
insights.so_what: Generic VLMs are essentially unusable for spatial grounding in driving scenes; this is the widest and most defensible moat in the disclosed results.
insights.locator: Evaluate VQA response and grounding quality

insights.claim: The auto-labeling pitch is that manual annotation of long-tail driving clips requires inspecting temporal and multi-camera context to identify causal actors, and that the model can compress annotation cycles from months to days.
insights.speaker: Boris Ivanovic
insights.so_what: A months-to-days claim on labeling is an existential threat to human AV annotation vendors and materially shortens AV development iteration cycles.
insights.quote: This can compress annotation cycles from months to days.
insights.locator: Auto-labeling

insights.claim: The model can auto-label clips lacking future trajectory data by first predicting its own future trajectory and feeding that back in as the observed future motion — a self-bootstrapping loop that removes the need for logged ground truth.
insights.speaker: Boris Ivanovic
insights.so_what: Self-supplied futures unlock labeling of arbitrary dashcam-grade video, hugely expanding the usable data pool — but the labels inherit the model's own biases.
insights.quote: Get the model to predict a future trajectory of its own, and use that in auto-labeling as the "observed" future motion.
insights.locator: By default, Alpamayo 2 Super assumes access

insights.claim: The published AlpaSim configuration flags that Alpamayo 2 Super is memory intensive with a recommended batch size of 1, and that enabling classifier-free guidance navigation sampling requires two GPUs with at least 70 GB VRAM each.
insights.speaker: Boris Ivanovic
insights.so_what: Two 70GB-plus GPUs to run one evaluation instance means the free model still requires datacenter-class NVIDIA hardware — the giveaway sells compute.
insights.quote: this requires 2 GPUs with at least 70 GB VRAM
insights.locator: Alpamayo 2 Super Driver Configuration for Alpasim

insights.claim: Perception spans 360 degrees across up to seven cameras with four temporal frames per camera, and the model uses language-only navigation rather than waypoint commands.
insights.speaker: Boris Ivanovic
insights.so_what: Language-only routing instead of waypoints is an architectural bet that natural language is the right control interface for driving — a break from conventional AV planning stacks.
insights.locator: Route configuration — A2Super uses language-only navigation
